rationale: C02 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both letters concern an Atomic Energy Commission scientific or technical achievement, characterize the successful completion as an exceptional accomplishment, and culminate in a request that an intermediary convey presidential congratulations or commendation to the responsible leader and all participating personnel. This combination of subject matter, rhetorical progression, and closely parallel conveyance language is substantially more distinctive than generic congratulatory correspondence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The completion of this machine...represents a significant scientific accomplishment
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The successful completion of this mission is an outstanding example of cooperation
shared_material.explanation: Both introduce the achievement through a parallel 'completion' formulation followed by an assessment of its exceptional significance.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Perhaps he would be kind enough to convey to Dr. Maurice Goldhaber...and to all the scientists and engineers who participated...my sincere congratulations.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Please convey to the Commander of Joint Task Force Seven and to all of the members...who contributed...my commendation
shared_material.explanation: The operative closing uses the same distinctive structure: ask an intermediary to convey presidential praise to the responsible leader and to all personnel who contributed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: By means of this and similar instruments of science, the United States...is making substantial strides
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the accomplishments of the Commission's Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory
shared_material.explanation: Both place the congratulatory message within the Atomic Energy Commission's scientific and technical work, reinforcing the structural and functional match.
